summary: This note is a short biographical entry on Karl Schiller, a German economist and Social Democratic Party (SPD) politician who lived from 1911 to 1994. It covers his ministerial posts in the late 1960s and early 1970s and his two named economic contributions: the "magic square" of economic equilibrium and "Concerted activity" for reflating the German market. The note describes him as one of the most influential German economists alongside Ludwig Erhard.
one_line: Biography of Karl Schiller, SPD economist and minister who devised the "magic square" of economic equilibrium.
key_facts: Karl August Fritz Schiller was born on 24 April 1911.
Karl August Fritz Schiller died on 26 December 1994.
Karl Schiller was a German economist and politician of the Social Democratic Party (SPD).
From 1966 to 1972, Karl Schiller was Federal Minister of Economic Affairs.
From 1971 to 1972, Karl Schiller was Federal Minister of Finance.
Karl Schiller was the inventor of the "magic square", depicting Economic equilibrium.
Karl Schiller was the inventor of the "Concerted activity" to reflate the German market.
Karl Schiller is seen as one of the most influential German economists beside Ludwig Erhard.
